newsitem.title: USA: U.S. execution held up because killer may be insane.
newsitem.headline: U.S. execution held up because killer may be insane.

text.p: A judge was to decide Wednesday if a man who spent 10 years on death row for torturing six women in his basement, feeding them human flesh and murdering two of them, was insane and therefore ineligible for execution.

Gary Heidnik, 53, was scheduled to die by lethal injection at 10 p.m. Tuesday when he received a stay of execution while U.S. District Judge Franklin Van Antwerpen considered his fate. The issue was whether Heidnik met federal criteria for the death penalty.

The judge heard psychiatric testimony into the early morning hours of Wednesday. Three defence witnesses told the judge Heidnik was delusional and believed he was the victim of a plot by his former captives.

Defence lawyers have also mounted an appeal in state court. Lawyers for the Centre for Legal Education, Advocacy and Defence Assistance will have the right to a state Supreme Court hearing Wednesday on their appeal if Heidnik is found mentally competent in federal court.
Heidnik was in a prison van headed for Rockview State Prison, the execution site, when the van was ordered to return to Philadelphia for the hearing.
Heidnik claimed insanity at his 1988 trial, but a jury convicted him and sentenced him to death.

Heidnik, whose residence was dubbed a "house of horrors" during his trial, kept six women in chains in his basement between November 1986 and March 1987. He was accused of dismembering the body of one woman who died of starvation and feeding some of her remains to the others.
Heidnik killed a second woman by attaching electrical wires to her chains while she stood in a pit filled with water.
Police arrested Heidnik in March 1987 after one woman escaped and led them to his home.

Police found body parts in Heidnik's freezer that belonged to the woman he dismembered. The second murder victim's body was found dumped in a state forest in New Jersey. The remaining three women were found alive.
If executed, he would be the third person to die since the state reinstated the death penalty.

During a three-hour hearing Monday the bearded Heidnik told Judge John Poserina Jr. he wanted to die to make the case against capital punishment. He said he had been convicted falsely and that the surviving captives killed the other two.
